newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on shortcovering, wheat.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on shortcovering, wheat.

text.p: Gains in wheat futures, coupled with fund shortcovering and commercial buying, spawned a higher close for CBOT corn futures, traders said.

"Funds were short December and they were just rolling them over," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International. "Funds started to cover shorts yesterday, today was the second day of it and it's usually a three day event."
An impressive upturn in soybeans Tuesday despite bearish USDA crop production numbers plus two sessions of gains in wheat captured attention.
"Corn is trying to follow beans and wheat, a little short covering and there's rolling of the December shorts forward," said Paul Haugens, vice president of Chicago-based trade house FIMAT Futures.

Corn Tuesday closed lower but found underpinning from aggressive commercial buying during the break early in the session. USDA Tuesday released its November crop production report which was considered bearish for corn futures.
Wednesday the market was attempting to consolidate.
Corn closed 1-1/2 to 3-3/4 cents higher, with December up 3-3/4 at $2.71-3/4 a bushel.
